title: Contextual per, ditto and reciprocal account references in a complete Pacioli posting
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED: the complete precious-stones teaching unit links opposed40/0/0/0 postings, Journal3/2 and index under contextual book/side roles. Wrong references may balance yet contradict ownership. Source1494 is later comparative evidence.

design.structural_baseline: Directed word composition, hierarchy at spaces, whole-form residuals and entry context are measured background; none identifies these external mechanisms. No confirmed word is required for an explicit future hypothesis.
design.access: Source-only; no target packet, image, reserved data, new admission, decoder, solver, statistics, process management, contact, refresh or commit.
design.whole_hypothesis: A complete account unit consists of a full transaction description and context-dependent linked postings. Inverse reading must reconstruct one transaction from all linked records, preserving host/counteraccount exchange, amount/date and description ownership.
design.source_date: Pacioli1494, directly owned through Geijsbeek1914 translation/facsimile; later than1450, no earlier exact writing-convention claim.
complete_unit_inventory: Declare the second entry as precious stones and choose Ledger space appropriate to expected account use; frequent cash/capital get larger space to reduce transfers.
Supply the year at page head only if not already present; inherited header must have an owner. Source does not repeat the year in the stones example.
Debit stones on the left, November8, counteraccount capital, referencing page2.
Retain different stone kinds, unspecified counts/weights, balassi/sapphires/rubies/unpolished diamonds, bulk versus separated kinds, value description and the printed40/0/0/0 amount.
Mark the Journal debit posting completed with its first diagonal line.
Credit capital under its earlier cash entry, using fewer words and a date ditto, pointing to stones page3, same40/0/0/0.
Mark the Journal credit posting with the other line; record debit-page3 above credit-page2; capital page2 remains until filled.
The example guides other cases; make the index entry immediately, underG orZ according to Gioie pronunciation, with VeniceZ and TuscanyG explicitly distinguished.

Keep supporting rules: paired amount, debit/credit roles, optional visual bar between page numbers, possible time gap between posting acts, journal as fuller explanation, and lost-ledger reconstruction.

attested_context_operations.per: Journal debtor marker but Ledger counteraccount introducer on both opposed sides. Account heading/side supplies the missing role.
attested_context_operations.ditto: Reuses an already provided date or description in its stated account context; not a universal nearest-noun pronoun.
attested_context_operations.page2_and_page3: Resolve to the other account in each posting; Journal stacked3/2 means debit-page/credit-page, not a rational number.
attested_context_operations.two_diagonals: Separate completion states for posting each half; legal temporary one-sided posting is not proof of final balance.
attested_context_operations.index_G_or_Z: Local pronunciation determines alternate indexing, without altering the transaction.

design.finite_content_contract: Fix one transaction object T with date, asset-description record, amount vector, debit account and credit account; create POST(T,host,side,counter-page,description-reference), with the two host/side assignments opposed. JOURNAL(T,debit-page,credit-page,debit-done,credit-done) and INDEX(account,page,initial-context) close the reference network. Source-defined description slots include kinds/count/weight/bulk-or-separated; written placeholders stay uninstantiated parameters. Meta-instructions for header, spacing, abbreviation, marking and indexing are separately retained semantic clauses. This is a finite typed analyst record, not a selected glyph code or a claim that Pacioli wrote this notation.
design.concrete_joint_consequence: Stones page3 debit per capital2 and capital page2 credit per stones3 must have identical date/value and refer to the same description. The Journal3/2 and index must resolve those same pages. None of the bare names, numeric total40 or isolated per occurrences establishes this alone.

different_rivals.rival: Read per as debtor in every book and on both sides.
different_rivals.consequence: Makes the capital credit entry misassign its written host/counteraccount roles.

different_rivals.rival: Swap only the Journal marginal3/2 to2/3.
different_rivals.consequence: Keeps all names, values and global debit-credit equality but reverses the claimed locations of the two accounts.

different_rivals.rival: Replace capital by another creditor with the same value.
different_rivals.consequence: Still balances but breaks the written stones-to-capital counterreference and index ownership.

different_rivals.rival: Make every ditto refer to the last word or latest arbitrary transaction.
different_rivals.consequence: Can change the date or object while preserving local token legality; loses the full shared-transaction reconstruction.

pitfalls: The teaching example has explicit unfilled quantities and general advice; a whole commercial history is not recovered.
Abbreviated descriptions depend on an accessible full Journal owner. Without it, several goods may have the same account/value and inversion is ambiguous.
Global renaming of account names/pages preserves relational structure until their writing is bound.
Balance alone never identifies economic roles or correct transaction labels.
Accounting identity is not physical stock identity or material conservation.
1494 is a chronology limitation; no pre1450 eligibility claimed.
No finite spelling realization for every explanatory sentence is provided; omitting that prose while calling the whole unit translated would be invalid.

predecessors.retained: Its required independently fixed physical final inventory remains missing. This is a different external crossrecord informational constraint, not reopening of the old material register.
No fixed additive character sum or one-source-record-per-target-line premise. Closed class unchanged.

design.smallest_future_decision: Before selection, identify an already admitted complete group of records with a finite full writer and genuine shared-description/counterreference capacity. A lone balanced pair with free labels is insufficient. No such target capacity is asserted here.
